mainTopic: רוב in דיני נפשות, the age at which a boy's intercourse counts, proofs that earlier generations fathered children at eight, and the start of 'a son, not a daughter'
overview: This amud opens by finishing רבי ירמיה מדפתי's proof that we follow the רוב even in דיני נפשות. The proof comes from the משנה about a married three-year-old girl, who might turn out to be an איילונית. The גמרא pushes back with several readings and ends by saying the husband accepted her no matter what, so the proof falls away. Next, a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a minor boy's intercourse with his mother. רב חסדא explains that they argue only about an eight-year-old: can we learn from earlier generations, when people fathered children at eight? The גמרא then hunts for a source for that fact. The proofs from אחיתופל's family and from הרן and שרה are both rejected. A proof from כלב, חור, אורי and בצלאל finally shows that each father had a child at eight. The amud ends by returning to the משנה's words 'a son, not a daughter,' where רבי שמעון begins a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that we follow the majority even for the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה מדפתי argues from the משנה about a married three-year-old girl. The man who sleeps with her is put to death even though she might be an איילונית, so we must be relying on the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he put to death? Say she is an איילונית, and the husband never meant to marry such a woman, so the marriage is void! Rather, isn't it because we say: go after the majority, and most women are not איילונית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that בית דין follows the majority even when a person's life is at stake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a girl turns out to be an איילונית, her קידושין may be a mistake, and then she was never an אשת איש. The משנה still gives the death penalty for sleeping with her. That only works if we assume, based on the majority, that she is a normal woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is physically underdeveloped and cannot have children
With this in mind, on this understanding
Rather, is it not that...: introduces the only explanation that makes sense

steps.confusionAlert: We cannot yet know whether a three-year-old is an איילונית. That is exactly why the doubt exists, and why only the majority can settle it.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, רוב can be used even to put someone to death. That is a major rule for דיני נפשות.

phrases.english: Why? Say: she is an ailonit,
phrases.notes: He's asking why the man who slept with this married three-year-old gets the death penalty, as the משנה says.

phrases.english: and on this understanding he did not betroth!
Rather, is it not that we say:
go after the majority,
and most women are not ailonit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי ירמיה מדפתי's proof begun on the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow the majority even in capital cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that a man who sleeps with a married three-year-old girl is put to death.

steps.title: Maybe 'liable' only means a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'Liable for her' in the משנה may mean he must bring a קרבן, not that he is put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'liable for her' in the משנה mean? A sacrifice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the משנה's word 'liable' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן חטאת for an accidental sin can be required even when relying on a majority. Taking a life is more serious. So if the משנה only means a קרבן, it proves nothing about the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: A sacrifice, here a חטאת for an accidental sin

phrases.english: No, what is the meaning of 'he is liable for her' that it teaches?
A sacrifice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה about the death penalty.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may refer only to a קרבן, not to death.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'executed because of her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection. The משנה clearly speaks of people being put to death because of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't the משנה teach 'they are executed because of her'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection by quoting a different line from the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not only say 'liable'. It also says 'executed because of her'. So it must be talking about the death penalty, not just a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't it teach? Quotes a source to challenge

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach 'they are executed because of her'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה refers only to a קרבן.

steps.title: Execution is for when her father sleeps with her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the death penalty in the משנה refers to a relative such as her father. That is incest, which does not depend on her marriage at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about where her father slept with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its rejection by placing the execution line in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her father sleeps with her, the sin is incest. That has nothing to do with whether her קידושין is valid, so the doubt about איילונית does not matter. The death penalty there needs no majority.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he slept with her

phrases.english: Where her father slept with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The execution in the משנה is for sleeping with her as an אשת איש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The execution is for incest by a relative, which does not depend on her marriage.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'any of the forbidden relations'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. The משנה says 'any one of all the עריות', and that includes an אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't it teach 'if any one of all the forbidden relations slept with her'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer about her father by pointing to the broad wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the עריות' sounds like every forbidden relationship, not just relatives. That would include sleeping with her as a married woman, so execution for אשת איש is back. The proof from רוב seems to return.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden sexual relationships listed in the Torah

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach 'if one slept with her
any one of all the forbidden relations'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״אִם בָּא עָלֶיהָ אֶחָד מִכׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the execution to her father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'All the עריות' includes אשת איש, not only relatives.

steps.title: The husband accepted her no matter what
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. The case is one where the husband agreed to marry her even if she turns out to be an איילונית, so there is no doubt that needs a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are we dealing with here? Where he accepted her upon himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'father' answer and explains the משנה as a special case. This removes the proof about רוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband accepted her even as an איילונית, her קידושין is valid either way. Anyone who sleeps with her is truly sleeping with an אשת איש and is put to death. No majority was needed, so רבי ירמיה מדפתי's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrowing of the case

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives death for sleeping with a married three-year-old. But that may be because the husband accepted her even as an איילונית, so this משנה does not prove that רוב is followed in דיני נפשות.

phrases.english: Rather, what are we dealing with here?
Where he accepted her upon himself.
phrases.notes: The husband agreed to keep her as his wife even if she turns out to be an איילונית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 with a new case, which defends the rejection of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Execution for אשת איש depends on assuming, by רוב, that she is not an איילונית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband accepted her in any case, so her marriage is certain and no רוב is needed.

steps.title: A minor son and his mother: does it disqualify her from marrying a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that בית שמאי say a minor's intercourse disqualifies the woman from כהונה, while בית הלל say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a woman acts lewdly with her young son and he begins intercourse with her, בית שמאי say he has made her unfit to marry a כהן. בית הלל say she is still fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about whether a minor boy's act counts as real intercourse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the boy's act counts as intercourse, the woman becomes forbidden to a כהן. בית שמאי treat it as real intercourse. בית הלל do not, because the boy is too young.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This opens a ברייתא.
Acting lewdly, behaving improperly in a sexual way
He made her unfit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A woman who acts lewdly with her minor son,
and he performed the initial stage of intercourse with her –
Beit Shammai say:
he has disqualified her from the priesthood,
and Beit Hillel deem her fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the legal status of a minor boy's intercourse, after the earlier discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: a minor's intercourse disqualifies the woman from כהונה. בית הלל: it does not.

steps.title: The argument is only about an eight-year-old
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא (some say in the name of זעירי) limits the מחלוקת. Everyone agrees that age nine and one day counts and that under eight does not. They argue only about age eight: can we learn from earlier generations?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בריה דרבה בר נחמני said in the name of רב חסדא (some say רב חסדא in the name of זעירי): Everyone agrees that a boy nine years and one day old counts for intercourse, and that a boy under eight does not. They argue only about an eight-year-old. בית שמאי think we learn from earlier generations, and בית הלל think we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא explains the ברייתא and narrows the argument down to one specific age, eight years old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא looked like a broad argument about any minor. רב חסדא shows that both sides agree on the edges, nine and up and under eight. The real question is whether the fact that people in early times could father children at eight still applies today.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say. This gives another version of who said it.
His intercourse counts as legal intercourse

steps.whatToRemember: Nine years and one day counts, and under eight does not. The only argument is about age eight, and it depends on whether we learn from earlier generations.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya, son of Rabba bar Nachmani, said:
Rav Chisda said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר זְעֵירִי:
phrases.english: and some say: Rav Chisda said that Ze'eiri said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבֶן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: All agree regarding a boy nine years and one day old
that his intercourse is considered intercourse,

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה שֶׁאֵין בִּיאָתוֹ בִּיאָה.
phrases.english: and that a boy less than eight years old, his intercourse is not considered intercourse.
They disagreed only about an eight-year-old,
as Beit Shammai hold:
we learn from the earlier generations,
and Beit Hillel hold:
we do not learn from the earlier generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבֶן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא's argument to the age of eight and explains the reasoning of each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine and one day counts and under eight does not. At eight, בית שמאי learn from earlier generations and בית הלל do not.

steps.title: How do we know earlier generations fathered children so young?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that people in earlier generations fathered children at around eight years old.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the earlier generations: how do we know that they fathered children at such a young age?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the fact that בית שמאי's opinion is built on. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's view only works if it is true that boys in early times could father children at eight. The גמרא wants a source for that fact before accepting it.

phrases.english: And the earlier generations,
from where do we know that they fathered children?
phrases.notes: He means at such a young age, around eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the factual basis of בית שמאי's reasoning given in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that people in earlier generations fathered children at about age eight.

steps.title: Building the family tree: בת שבע, אחיתופל and the birth of שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof from verses. בת שבע was אחיתופל's granddaughter, and then שלמה was born to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we know it from these verses: 'Is this not בת שבע, daughter of אליעם, wife of אוריה the Hittite?' and 'אליעם son of אחיתופל the Gilonite,' and 'He sent by the hand of נתן the prophet, and he called his name ידידיה, for the sake of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts suggesting a source by lining up verses. The goal is to work out how young each generation in אחיתופל's family was when they had children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two verses show that בת שבע was אחיתופל's granddaughter. The third verse marks the birth of שלמה (ידידיה) to her. That birth becomes the starting point for a timeline. The word אילימא shows this is a suggested source that the גמרא is testing.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This introduces a suggested answer that may be questioned.
From what is written in a פסוק
ידידיה, another name given to שלמה

phrases.english: If you say, from that which is written:
"Is this not Bathsheba,
daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 11:3

phrases.english: And it is written: "Eliam, son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:34. Put together, these two verses make בת שבע the granddaughter of אחיתופל.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet,
and he called his name Jedidiah,
for the sake of (for) the Lord (loved him)."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:25. The verse itself just says 'for the sake of ה׳', so some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִדִּכְתִיב: ״הֲלוֹא זֹאת בַּת שֶׁבַע בַּת אֱלִיעָם אֵשֶׁת אוּרִיָּה הַחִתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of Step 9 with a timeline built from verses.
steps.raayaObject: That earlier generations fathered children at a very young age.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Verses in שמואל ב linking בת שבע to אחיתופל and marking the birth of שלמה.

steps.title: Counting the years after שלמה's birth: אבשלום's sheepshearing and his escape
steps.stepSummary: The proof continues. Two years passed until אבשלום's sheepshearing, and then he spent three years in גשור, so five years after שלמה's birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'It was after two full years that אבשלום had sheepshearers.' And it is written: 'אבשלום fled and went to גשור, and was there three years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps adding verses to count the years that passed after שלמה was born. The timeline is still being built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheepshearing, when אמנון was killed, came two years later. Then אבשלום fled for three more years. That adds up to five years after שלמה's birth, and the count will be used to work out how young אחיתופל's family members were when they had children.

keyTerms.meaning: To גשור, the place where אבשלום fled

phrases.english: And it is written: "And it came to pass after two full years
that Absalom had sheepshearers,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:23. This is the event where אמנון was killed.

phrases.english: And it is written: "So Absalom fled and went to Geshur,
and was there three years."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:38. Two years plus three years: we are now five years after שלמה's birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי לִשְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים וַיִּהְיוּ גֹזְזִים לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the timeline from Step 10 by counting the years after שלמה's birth.
steps.raayaObject: The timeline needed to show that early generations fathered children very young.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 13:23 and 13:38, which give two years and then three years.

steps.title: Counting to seven years and the death of אחיתופל
steps.stepSummary: Two more years in ירושלים bring the count to seven years after שלמה's birth. אבשלום's rebellion then begins, and during it אחיתופל strangles himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written that אבשלום lived two years in ירושלים without seeing the king. That brings us to seven years after שלמה was born. Then it is written that אבשלום asked to go to חברון, which is the start of his rebellion. During the rebellion, אחיתופל saw that his advice was ignored, so he went home and strangled himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps adding up years from the פסוקים. It shows that when אחיתופל died, שלמה was about seven years old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 reached five years after שלמה's birth. The two years in ירושלים bring the total to seven. The rebellion, and אחיתופל's death during it, came after that, so שלמה was at least seven when אחיתופל died.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's son, who rebelled against him
A vow. אבשלום used paying a vow as his excuse to go to חברון
Advice. אחיתופל's advice to אבשלום was not followed

phrases.english: And it is written: "And Absalom lived in Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים וּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא רָאָה״.
phrases.english: two full years, and he did not see the king's face."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 14:28. Counting all the years since שלמה was born, we're now at seven.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And it was at the end of forty years
that Absalom said to the king:
Please let me go and pay my vow
that I vowed to ה׳, in Hebron."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:7. This trip to חברון is where אבשלום's rebellion starts.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל רָאָה כִּי לֹא נֶעֶשְׂתָה עֲצָתוֹ
phrases.english: And it is written: "And Achitophel saw that his advice was not followed,
and he saddled the donkey and got up,
and went to his house, to his city,
and gave instructions to his household, and strangled himself."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 17:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the year count from step 11, from five years up to seven, and ends at אחיתופל's death.
steps.raayaObject: That people in earlier generations fathered children at about eight

steps.title: אחיתופל lived only thirty-three years
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says wicked men do not live half their days, and a ברייתא says אחיתופל lived only 33 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written that men of blood and deceit do not live out half their days. A ברייתא teaches that דואג lived only 34 years and אחיתופל lived only 33.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second number it needs for the calculation: how old אחיתופל was when he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal lifespan is 70, so half is 35. The ברייתא shows that both of these wicked men died before 35. This gives a fixed age for אחיתופל's death: 33.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked advisor of שאול, mentioned here alongside אחיתופל
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And it is written: "Men of blood and deceit
will not live out half their days."
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:24

phrases.english: And it was taught: All the years of Doeg
were only thirty-four,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל אֲחִיתֹפֶל אֵינָן אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: and those of Achitophel were only thirty-three.
phrases.notes: Both died before 35, which is half of a normal 70 years. That matches the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds אחיתופל's age at death, which is needed for the math.

steps.title: The math: each generation had a child at eight
steps.stepSummary: 33 minus 7 leaves 26. Subtracting two years for three pregnancies leaves 24 years for three generations, so each parent had a child at eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: How old was אחיתופל? Thirty-three. Subtract seven, which was שלמה's age then, and 26 years are left. Subtract two years for three pregnancies, and it turns out that each parent had a child at age eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the numbers together and reaches its result: in those generations, people had children at eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between אחיתופל's birth and שלמה's birth there are three generations: אחיתופל to אליעם, אליעם to בת שבע, and בת שבע to שלמה. That span was 26 years, and about two of those years were pregnancies. That leaves 24 years for three generations, or eight years each.

phrases.english: How many years did he have?
Thirty-three.
Subtract seven, which was Solomon's age,
and twenty-six are left.
Subtract two years for three pregnancies,

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתְּכַח דְּכֹל חַד וְחַד בְּתַמְנֵי אוֹלֵיד.
phrases.english: and it turns out that each one had a child at eight.
phrases.notes: The three are אחיתופל (father of אליעם), אליעם (father of בת שבע), and בת שבע (mother of שלמה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the year count from steps 10-12 with the age from step 13 to finish the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That people in earlier generations had children at eight
steps.raayaSupportSource: The year calculation from the פסוקים and the ברייתא

steps.title: Maybe two fathers at nine and a mother at six
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the 24 years could be split as nine, nine and six, since a woman matures faster. Support: בת שבע had an earlier child.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe both men had children at nine, and בת שבע gave birth at six, because a woman develops faster. You can see this is true, because she had already had a child before שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from אחיתופל's family by showing another way the numbers could work out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 24 years do not have to be split evenly as 8+8+8. They could be 9+9+6, and then no man had a child at eight. בת שבע's earlier child shows that she gave birth even younger than when she had שלמה, so a very young mother is believable.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? It challenges a proof
Know that it is so; it brings support

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not deny that בת שבע had a child very young. It only says the men may have been nine, not eight, so the proof about men at eight falls away.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps both of them fathered children at nine,
phrases.notes: He means אחיתופל and his son אליעם.

phrases.english: and Bathsheba gave birth at six,
because a woman is stronger.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע, דְּהָא הֲוַי לַהּ וָלָד מֵעִיקָּרָא.
phrases.english: Know that this is so, for she had a child even before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the calculation of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from אחיתופל's family
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 24 years can be divided unevenly (9, 9, 6), so it does not show that a man fathered a child at eight.

steps.title: A new proof begins from תרח's sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof: אברהם was a year older than נחור, and נחור a year older than הרן, so אברהם was two years older than הרן. Then אברם and נחור took wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from here: תרח fathered אברם, נחור and הרן. אברהם was a year older than נחור, and נחור was a year older than הרן, so אברהם was two years older than הרן. And it is written that אברם and נחור took wives.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first proof, the גמרא begins a new one. Here it lays out the brothers' ages, setting up a calculation that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new proof uses the ages of תרח's sons: הרן was two years younger than אברהם. The פסוק about the brothers marrying is mentioned because נחור's wife was הרן's daughter. That fact will be used to show how young הרן was when he had children.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here; starts a new proof after the old one failed
It comes out, it turns out

phrases.english: Rather, learn it from here:
"These are the generations of Terah:

phrases.aramaic: תֶּרַח הוֹלִיד אֶת אַבְרָם אֶת נָחוֹר וְאֶת הָרָן״.
phrases.english: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran."
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:27

phrases.english: And Abraham was older than Nahor by a year,
and Nahor was older than Haran by a year.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אַבְרָהָם גָּדוֹל שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים מֵהָרָן.
phrases.english: So Abraham was two years older than Haran.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּקַּח אַבְרָם וְנָחוֹר לָהֶם נָשִׁים וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: And it is written: "And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves, and so on."
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:29. The rest of the פסוק says נחור's wife מלכה was הרן's daughter. That is the key to the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in step 15, a new proof answers the question of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That people in earlier generations fathered children at about eight

steps.title: Iscah is Sarah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק identifies יסכה, daughter of הרן, as שרה. He gives two reasons for the name: she saw through רוח הקודש, or everyone gazed at her beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: יסכה is שרה. Why was she called יסכה? Because she 'saw' through רוח הקודש. That is why the פסוק says, 'All that שרה tells you, listen to her voice.' Another explanation: she was called יסכה because everyone gazed at her beauty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יצחק's teaching that יסכה, the daughter of הרן, is the same person as שרה. This sets up the age calculation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק from step 16 says הרן was the father of מלכה and יסכה. If יסכה is שרה, then שרה was הרן's daughter. That link is what lets the גמרא measure how old הרן was when he had her.

keyTerms.meaning: Iscah, a daughter of הרן; here identified as שרה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
"Iscah" is Sarah,
phrases.notes: יסכה is named in the פסוק about הרן's daughters (בראשית 11:29), so this makes שרה הרן's daughter.

phrases.english: and why was she called "Iscah"?
Because she saw by means of divine inspiration.
phrases.notes: סוכה means 'looks' or 'sees', which sounds like the name יסכה.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"All that Sarah says to you,
listen to her voice."
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:12

phrases.english: Another explanation: "Iscah"
because everyone gazed at her beauty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the identity link (יסכה is שרה) needed to turn the brothers' ages from step 16 into a proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יסכה, daughter of הרן, is שרה.

steps.title: Haran had Sarah at age eight
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק shows אברהם was ten years older than שרה. Since he was two years older than הרן, הרן fathered שרה at eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'אברהם fell on his face and laughed and said in his heart...' (shall a man of 100 have a child, and שרה at 90 give birth?). So how much older was אברהם than שרה? Ten years. And he was two years older than her father הרן. It turns out that הרן fathered שרה at age eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second proof. It does the math to show that הרן had a child at age eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the פסוק says אברהם was 100 and שרה 90, so he was ten years older. Step 16 said אברהם was two years older than הרן. Ten minus two means הרן was only eight when שרה was born.

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And Abraham fell on his face
and laughed, and said in his heart, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:17. The rest of the פסוק says אברהם is 100 and שרה is 90.

phrases.english: How much older was Abraham than Sarah?
Ten years.
And he was two years older than her father.
phrases.notes: That is הרן. The two-year gap was worked out in step 16.

phrases.english: It turns out that when Haran fathered Sarah,
he fathered her at eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתְּכַח כִּי אוֹלְדַהּ הָרָן לְשָׂרָה בְּתַמְנֵי אוֹלְדַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the identification of step 17 together with the ages from step 16 to complete the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can father a child at age eight.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 17:17 (ages 100 and 90), combined with the birth order of תרח's sons.

steps.title: Maybe Abraham was the youngest brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. אברהם may have been the youngest, and the פסוק lists the brothers by wisdom, not by age.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe אברהם was the youngest of his brothers, and the פסוק lists them in the order of their wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof. It questions the idea that אברהם was the oldest just because he is named first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole calculation depended on אברהם being older than הרן. If the order in the פסוק reflects wisdom and not age, אברהם might be younger than הרן. Then הרן could have been much older when שרה was born, and the proof collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: In the order of their wisdom

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps Abraham was the youngest of his brothers,
and the verse lists them in the order of their wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא אַבְרָהָם זוּטָא דַּאֲחוּהּ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 16-18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire second proof that a child can be fathered at eight.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the order of names in the פסוק is birth order. That order may reflect wisdom instead.

steps.title: Proof from Noah's sons that the verse lists by wisdom
steps.stepSummary: שם is listed first among נח's sons. But the numbers show he could not be the oldest. If he were, he would have been 102, not 100, two years after the מבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that the פסוק lists them by wisdom. It is written: 'נח was 500 years old, and נח fathered שם, חם and יפת.' If listed by age, שם is a year older than חם, and חם a year older than יפת, so שם is two years older than יפת. It is also written: 'נח was 600 years old when the flood came.' And: 'שם was 100 years old when he fathered ארפכשד, two years after the flood.' Only 100? He would have been 102!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection. It shows a clear case where the תורה lists brothers out of age order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שם were the oldest, born when נח was 500, he would be 100 at the מבול and 102 two years later. But the פסוק says he was 100 then. So שם must have been born when נח was 502, which makes him the youngest, even though he is listed first.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume שם was 'two years older' as a fact. That line is only what we would say if the list were by age, and the גמרא is showing it leads to a contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ קְרָא דֶּרֶךְ חׇכְמָתָן,
phrases.english: Know that the verse lists them in the order of their wisdom,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי נֹחַ בֶּן חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
phrases.english: as it is written: "And Noah was five hundred years old,

phrases.aramaic: וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ אֶת שֵׁם אֶת חָם וְאֶת יָפֶת״.
phrases.english: and Noah fathered Shem, Ham and Japheth."
phrases.notes: בראשית 5:32

phrases.english: Shem is a year older than Ham,
and Ham is a year older than Japheth.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא שֵׁם גָּדוֹל מִיֶּפֶת שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: It comes out that Shem is two years older than Japheth.
And it is written: "And Noah was six hundred years old
when the flood was water upon the earth."
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:6

phrases.english: And it is written: "(These are) the descendants of Shem:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁם בֶּן מְאַת שָׁנָה וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת אַרְפַּכְשָׁד
phrases.english: Shem was a hundred years old and fathered Arpachshad
two years after the flood."
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:10

phrases.english: A hundred years old?
He was a hundred and two years old!
phrases.notes: If שם was born when נח was 500, he was 100 at the flood and 102 two years later.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ קְרָא דֶּרֶךְ חׇכְמָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 19 by showing the תורה does list brothers by wisdom.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק sometimes lists brothers by wisdom rather than by age.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 5:32, 7:6 and 11:10: the ages of נח and שם around the מבול.

steps.title: Here too the list may follow wisdom
steps.stepSummary: Since the list of נח's sons follows wisdom, the list of תרח's sons may too. So the proof that הרן had שרה at eight fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it lists them in the order of their wisdom. Here too, it lists them in the order of their wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the rejection. It applies the lesson from נח's sons back to אברהם and his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נח's sons, the only way to fit the numbers is that שם, listed first, was really the youngest. The same can be true of אברהם. Once his being the oldest is uncertain, the age-eight calculation for הרן no longer holds.
steps.whatToRemember: The second proof (from הרן and שרה) is rejected. The order of names in a פסוק does not always show who was born first; sometimes it shows who was wiser.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דֶּרֶךְ חׇכְמָתָן קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ.
phrases.english: Rather, it lists them in the order of their wisdom.
Here too,
it lists them in the order of their wisdom.
phrases.notes: He means תרח's sons: אברהם may be named first for his wisdom, not his age.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דֶּרֶךְ חׇכְמָתָן קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ. הָכָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 20 and applies it to the case of אברהם and הרן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the תורה may list brothers by wisdom, אברהם may not be older than הרן, so there is no proof that הרן fathered שרה at eight.

steps.title: A simpler verse shows יפת was the oldest
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רב זביד learned from a פסוק, not from the math, that יפת was the oldest of נח's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I repeated this teaching before רב זביד of נהרדעא. He told me: You learn it from that source, but we learn it from this verse: 'And to שם, the father of all the children of עבר, the brother of יפת the elder, children were born to him too.' So יפת was the oldest of the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another way to prove that שם was not the oldest son. רב זביד says a פסוק states it openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20 the גמרא used the ages and years to show שם could not be the oldest. רב זביד reads the words 'יפת הגדול', 'יפת the big one', to mean יפת was the oldest. The conclusion of Step 21 stays the same, but now it rests on a plain verse instead of a calculation.

keyTerms.meaning: The big one; here it means the oldest

phrases.english: Rav Kahana says:
I said this teaching
before Rav Zevid of Neharde'a.
He said to me: You learn it from that source,
phrases.notes: He means the age calculation from Step 20.

phrases.english: and we learn it from here:
"And to Shem, children were also born to him,
the father of all the children of Ever,
the brother of Yefes the elder."
phrases.notes: בראשית 10:21

phrases.english: Yefes was the oldest of his brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן מֵהָכָא מַתְנִיתוּ, וַאֲנַן מֵהָכָא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, simpler source for the point proven by calculation in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That יפת, not שם, was the oldest son of נח

steps.title: So where do we learn fathering at age eight?
steps.stepSummary: Since the proof from הרן fell, the גמרא asks for a new source that people once fathered children at eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for a new source, because the proof from הרן and שרה was taken away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that a child of eight could father a child still needs a source. Step 21 showed the הרן proof is not reliable. So the גמרא looks for a different proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; used when an earlier idea has failed
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Rather, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: Know what? That people back then fathered children at age eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question after the side point about נח's sons.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A valid source that a person could father a child at age eight

steps.title: בצלאל's family line and his age at the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that בצלאל descended from כלב through חור and אורי. He was 13 when he built the משכן, and the spies were sent the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here: 'And בצלאל son of אורי son of חור, of the tribe of יהודה.' And it is written: 'עזובה, the wife of כלב, died, and כלב took אפרת, and she bore him חור.' How old was בצלאל when he made the משכן? Thirteen, since the verse calls the workers 'every man.' And a ברייתא teaches: in the first year משה made the משכן, and in the second year he set it up and sent the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its new proof by gathering the facts it needs: who בצלאל's ancestors were and how old he was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the two verses together gives four generations: כלב, then חור, then אורי, then בצלאל. Being called 'איש' (a man) means בצלאל was at least 13 while making the משכן. The ברייתא adds that the spies went out one year later, so he was 14 by then.

keyTerms.meaning: The portable Sanctuary in the desert
A man; here it means someone at least 13
The spies sent to check out ארץ ישראל
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: From here:
"And Betzalel son of Uri son of Chur
of the tribe of Yehuda,"
phrases.notes: שמות 38:22

phrases.english: And it is written: "And Azuva, the wife of Kalev, died,
and Kalev took Efras for himself,
and she bore him Chur."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:19. So the family line is כלב, then חור, then אורי, then בצלאל.

phrases.english: And when Betzalel made the Mishkan,
how old was he?
Thirteen, as it is written:
"Every man from his work
that they were doing."
phrases.notes: שמות 36:4. The workers are called 'man,' and you are only called a man from thirteen.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא: שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה מִשְׁכָּן,
phrases.english: And it was taught: In the first year Moshe made the Mishkan;
in the second year he set up the Mishkan
and sent the spies.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהָכָא: וּבְצַלְאֵל בֶּן אוּרִי בֶן חוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of Step 23 by setting out the family line and the timeline.
steps.raayaObject: That people fathered children at age eight
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 38:22, דברי הימים א 2:19, שמות 36:4, and a ברייתא about the years of the משכן

steps.title: The math: three generations in 24 years
steps.stepSummary: כלב was 40 when the spies were sent, and בצלאל was 14. Subtract 2 years for three pregnancies, and each father had his child at eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'I was forty years old when משה, the servant of ה׳, sent me,' and 'Now I am eighty-five years old today.' How old was כלב then? Forty. Take away the fourteen years of בצלאל, and twenty-six are left. Take away two years for three pregnancies. It turns out that each one fathered a child at eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by doing the math with כלב's age. It shows that each father in the line had his son at age eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב, בצלאל's great-grandfather, was only 40 when the spies were sent, while בצלאל was already 14. That leaves 26 years for כלב to father חור, חור to father אורי, and אורי to father בצלאל. After taking off about two years for three pregnancies, 24 years are left for three generations, which is 8 years each.
steps.whatToRemember: 40 − 14 − 2 = 24 years for three generations (כלב, חור, אורי), so each one fathered a child at eight. This replaces the rejected proof from הרן.
steps.confusionAlert: The 85 years is not part of the math. The number that matters is 40, כלב's age when the spies were sent.

phrases.english: And it is written: "I was forty years old
when Moshe the servant of ה׳ sent me, etc.,"
phrases.notes: יהושע 14:7. כלב is the one speaking.

phrases.english: "And now, here I am today
eighty-five years old."
phrases.notes: יהושע 14:10

phrases.english: How many years are there? Forty.
Take away the fourteen that Betzalel was,
phrases.notes: He was 13 at the building and one year older when the spies went, so 14.

phrases.english: twenty-six are left.
Take away two years for three pregnancies,
it turns out that each and every one
fathered a child at eight.
phrases.notes: 24 years shared by three fathers (כלב, חור, אורי) is 8 years each.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the facts from Step 24 together with כלב's age to complete the calculation.
steps.raayaObject: That people fathered children at age eight
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 14:7 and 14:10, combined with the timeline from Step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each of כלב, חור and אורי fathered a son at age eight.

steps.title: A son and not a daughter: רבי שמעון's logic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'a son, not a daughter' and begins a ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון says logic would treat a daughter like a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A son, and not a daughter.' It was taught: רבי שמעון said: By logic, a daughter should be fit to be treated like a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It goes back to the משנה's rule that only a son, not a daughter, can become a בן סורר ומורה, and it begins a ברייתא about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון begins by saying that, from logic alone, a daughter would seem to belong in this law as well. The ברייתא continues past this point, so the reason for this idea and the final halacha come later.

keyTerms.meaning: A son and not a daughter (quoted from the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not giving the final halacha here. He only says what logic would suggest, and the ברייתא goes on after this.

phrases.english: "A son, and not a daughter."
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
By logic, a daughter should
be fit to be like a stubborn and rebellious son,

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּן, וְלֹא בַּת. תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about fathering children young and goes back to the next words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה limits בן סורר ומורה to a son. רבי שמעון begins by noting that logic alone would include a daughter.
